Search results mix three separate jobs: Developer Program signup, App Store Connect metadata, and en-US marketing copy. If your blocker is “Apple rejected my organization verification” or “Paid Apps Agreement is greyed out,” rewriting your subtitle in Chinese will not unblock payouts. Conversely, a finished D-U-N-S match does not replace an English product page US buyers understand. Keep enrollment, Connect agreements, and listing localization in separate buckets.

1. Individual vs organization enrollment

  • Individual — enroll under your personal legal name in a country Apple supports; seller name on the App Store is typically your name unless you qualify for other display rules
  • Organization — enroll under a registered company, nonprofit, or other legal entity; seller name can be the organization brand when Apple accepts your documents
  • Team roles (Admin, App Manager, Developer) attach after the account exists — plan who holds the Admin role before you pay the annual Program fee
  • Switching entity type later is painful; pick based on how you actually invoice, sign contracts, and answer tax questions — not because a blog post said “always incorporate in Delaware”

We do not register companies, file incorporation paperwork, or impersonate you in Apple’s identity verification. The Ship from Asia pack explains decision points and document order — it is not done-for-you enrollment.

2. D-U-N-S — when Asia indie teams lose a week

  • Apple often requires a D-U-N-S Number for organization enrollments so Apple can match your legal entity name and address
  • Free D-U-N-S lookup through Dun & Bradstreet can take several business days; typos in legal name or address on your registration certificate cause mismatches
  • Sole developers enrolling as individuals usually skip D-U-N-S — verify current Apple Developer Program enrollment text for your country
  • If you already have D-U-N-S from a prior job or parent company, confirm the legal entity on the number matches the entity you are enrolling — not a co-founder’s old side LLC

We do not request D-U-N-S on your behalf or guarantee Dun & Bradstreet turnaround. Build slack into launch dates.

3. Entity country — local registration vs “US company” myths

  • Most Asia indie developers enroll with an entity or individual identity tied to their home jurisdiction and still distribute on the US App Store storefront
  • Forming a US LLC or C-Corp “for Apple” introduces separate tax, banking, and compliance work — this shop does not sell US company formation or registered-agent services
  • Apple’s enrollment portal asks for legal name, address, and phone that match government IDs or business registration documents — fictional US mailboxes fail verification
  • If you already operate under a Singapore, Hong Kong, or other regional entity, enroll that entity — do not spin up a parallel shell company without counsel

Entity choice is between you, Apple, and qualified professionals. This page orients you on what Connect typically expects — not which country you should incorporate in.

4. After enrollment — Paid Apps, tax forms, payout banking

  • Sign the Paid Apps Agreement in App Store Connect before selling paid downloads or IAP — the agreement stays inactive until tax and banking sections are complete
  • Complete tax forms Apple requests (often US W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E for non-US entities, depending on structure and treaty status)
  • Add payout banking Connect accepts for your region — many Asia teams use local accounts; some use multi-currency fintech accounts where permitted
  • Withholding, VAT, and corporate tax reporting stay with you and your advisors — we do not file on your behalf

High-level orientation only. Read Apple’s tax and banking help inside Connect and consult qualified tax or legal counsel for your jurisdiction.

5. Only after the account works — US storefront listing

Enrollment and agreements unlock Connect; they do not write your en-US title or screenshots. Once Paid Apps is active, you still need bundle ID alignment, privacy nutrition labels, and US-facing listing assets before review. That ship order is a different checklist from D-U-N-S — see our Connect guide, not AppLocale.

FAQ

Do I need a US company to enroll in the Apple Developer Program from Asia?

Usually no. Many indie developers enroll as an individual or a legal entity registered in their home country and still sell on the US App Store storefront. Apple’s required documents and verification steps vary by country — read Apple Developer Program enrollment for your region. This page is not legal or immigration advice, and we do not form US companies for you.

What is a D-U-N-S number and when does Apple ask for it?

A D-U-N-S number is a business identifier Dun & Bradstreet assigns to legal entities. Apple typically requires it when you enroll as an organization (company, nonprofit, etc.), not for a sole individual account in most regions. Lookup and matching can take days — plan before a hard launch deadline. The Ship from Asia pack walks through where D-U-N-S fits in the enrollment order; we do not obtain a D-U-N-S on your behalf.
